title: Fleet wavechart & velocity log — regional onboarding (NA/EU/APAC) H2 2026
summary: Operational sprint-friendly wavechart for onboarding GPU capacity across North America, Europe, and APAC for H2 2026. Includes per-wave velocity targets, SKU mix, prewarm buffer policy, and a short risk triage log intended for infra leads and SRE on-call.
background: We expect a demand inflection from hosted customers beginning Sept 2026 due to new feature launches and renewed enterprise commitments. This sheet converts that demand signal into a pragmatic wave-based onboarding plan that can be executed within cloud vendor provisioning windows and our internal templated runbooks.
assumptions: Demand scenario: +45% peak Q4 token throughput vs baseline (May 2026).
Preferred GPU SKUs: H100 where available; fall back to A100 80GB in constrained zones.
Each H100 node (1xH100-80GB equivalent) = ~12 rps for generation workload A; A100 node = ~8 rps.
Prewarm target: maintain 8% regional idle buffer during normal cadence, 12% during first 4 weeks post-wave launch.
Lead time for cold capacity from contracted cloud accounts = 18–28 days depending on zone.
Autoscaler can absorb up to 20% variance within a wave if bursting to spare vendor pools is enabled.
On-prem and private customers are excluded from this wave and scheduled separately.
wave_calendar: Wave 0 (prep): 2026-07-20 -> 2026-08-09 — validation, AMI bake, canary models in NA-west, EU-west clusters.
Wave 1: 2026-08-10 -> 2026-08-31 — NA core expansion (3 AZs). Target +320 H100-equivalent GPUs (primary placement NA-west/NA-east).
Wave 2: 2026-09-01 -> 2026-09-22 — EU rollout (2 zones). Target +220 H100-equivalent GPUs (mix H100:A100 = 70:30).
Wave 3: 2026-09-23 -> 2026-10-14 — APAC staged (SG/Tokyo). Target +180 H100-equivalent GPUs; priority for lower-latency regions for enterprise customers.
Wave 4 (buffer wave): 2026-10-15 -> 2026-11-05 — overflow capacity and cross-region failover lanes. Target +100 GPUs convertible between regions.
Contingency window: 2026-11-06 -> 2026-12-01 — vendor replacement/resizing and reserved capacity settlement.
region_forecast: North America (NA): Baseline H100-equivalent = 900 GPUs (May 2026). H2 incremental target = +420 -> projected EOP H2 = 1320. Monthly cadence: Aug +320, Oct +100 for buffer and late demand.
Europe (EU): Baseline = 480 GPUs. H2 incremental target = +220 -> projected EOP H2 = 700. Monthly cadence: Sep +220 (single staged wave across 2 zones).
APAC: Baseline = 320 GPUs. H2 incremental target = +180 -> projected EOP H2 = 500. Monthly cadence: Sep (staged) +120, Oct +60 for enterprise onboards and latency-critical placements.
node_mix_and_sku_strategy: Target SKU split (incremental H2): H100 75%, A100 25% (fallback).
Instance types: prefer 1xH100-80GB pods with 512GB host RAM templates for large-chat workloads; A100 80GB used where H100 allocation fails.
Quantized model highway: reserve 30% of incremental nodes for int8/4 workloads (cost-optimized pool) — annotated as 'Q-pool' in the console.
Burst pool: label up to 10% as 'burst' convertible capacity that can be repurposed between caching and live inference during peak events.
prewarm_policy: Prewarm steps are strictly enforced for each wave: (1) AMI & container validation in Wave 0, (2) warm KV/cache with 72-hour synthetic traffic for first half of the wave, (3) increase warm buffer to 12% for first 28 days after the wave starts, (4) observe token latency & tail p95 for 72 hours before marking wave as live. If p95 increases >20% vs baseline, rollback threshold triggers automated scale down and ticket to on-call.
capacity_risks: Vendor SKU shortage in EU zone during calendar weeks 36–38 (historical vendor maintenance windows).
Unexpected billing/quotas causing delayed attach of reserved instances (lead time slips to +35 days).
Cold-start latency degradation if prewarm is skipped or synthetic traffic insufficient.
Inter-region network egress limits during cross-region failover tests impacting cache repopulation times.
mitigations: Pre-book A100 fallbacks and negotiate credit-triggered swaps with vendors for EU (contact vendor-ops by 2026-07-01).
Parallelize provisioning by starting EU procurement immediately after Wave 0 finish; allow APAC to re-use NA templates to shave 3–5 days from lead time.
Increase prewarm synthetic traffic profile (10% heavier tails) for first two waves to detect p95 risks earlier.
Enable staged egress throttles and monitor cache warm rates during DR rehearsals; schedule failover drill in Wave 4 buffer window.
operational_checklist: Week -4: finalize SKU confirmations with cloud vendor and sign off capacity PO.
Week -3: bake AMIs, run integration tests against canary model path in NA-west.
Week -2: run synthetic warm traffic, validate KV cache warming and snapshotting.
Week 0: deploy wave into 1 AZ, observe for 72 hours, run traffic ramp to target RPS.
Week +2: evaluate telemetry, capacity economics, and optionally convert Q-pool nodes to live inference if utilization <60%.
Ongoing: SRE 24/7 coverage during first 7 days of each wave; rotate infra leads for handoff.
action_items: Sasha: finalize vendor PO for EU fallback (due 2026-03-05).
Diego: update autoscaler policies to allow 20% burst across zones and add 'burst' label (due 2026-03-12).
Ava: create canary test manifest and synthetic traffic profiles for Wave 0 (due 2026-03-01).
Priya: schedule DR failover drill for Wave 4 buffer window and publish runbook (due 2026-03-22).
metrics_and_acceptance: Primary SLOs: tail latency p95 < 420ms for generation workloads; sustained throughput targets reached within 36 hours of wave start.
Cost guardrails: incremental cost per 1k tokens should not exceed projected benchmark by >12% after quantization mix applied.
Operational acceptance: zero Sev1 incidents attributable to provisioning during first 72 hours for each wave.
notes: This sheet is intentionally sprint-oriented: waves are sized to match typical vendor lead-time batches and our infra team's 3-week sprint rhythm.
If vendor lead-times shorten unexpectedly, we can compress Wave 3 and Wave 4 by shifting 30% of APAC capacity into late-September window — requires signoff from finance for accelerated spend.
Keep this doc as the single source-of-truth for scheduling communiques to GTM and CS teams; do not create parallel spreadsheets without a clear merge plan.
